scope: One C++ fixture source; no production or workflow edits. No compilation or test rerun by reviewer.

documentation.section: Enhanced Socket Security: Windows Server 2003 and later, both bind calls under the same user account

reviewedBoundaries: Both sockets are created in one process, hence the same user context. AF_INET/TCP and SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE are set before bind. No SO_REUSEADDR was added.

The holder remains wildcard with an independently assigned nonzero port. The contender explicitly chooses INADDR_ANY or INADDR_LOOPBACK, converts the address with htonl and the port with htons. The loopback case matches the specific-interface table column.

The two original wildcard cases remain, each requiring10048. Two loopback-specific cases require10013. Both bound-not-listening and listening modes verify SO_ACCEPTCONN before the contention call; no success code or alternative error is silently accepted.

The unchanged real bind policy must call exactly [occupied,0], preserve immediate WSAGetLastError and both errors, choose a distinct nonzero endpoint, and keep that listener port across three bounded loopback connects/accepts. Invalid SOCKET must yield10038 with one attempt and no retry.

Observed firstError/fallbackError/success/retry count are flushed before the merged assertion, so a future mismatch retains the actual numeric result. A failed fallback does not call getsockname on an unbound socket.

Socket handles have RAII destructors. Blocking holder, server and each client unwind on require exceptions; each successfully accepted peer is closed before later checks. WSA cleanup occurs after socket-local frames unwind. The connect is nonblocking with two-second select checks and SO_ERROR verification; original cleanup policy is preserved.
The seven portable policy cases and require-based checks are unchanged and stay active with NDEBUG. Native main invokes four address/listen combinations plus invalid-socket, for five Windows cases.
